## 040 · Integration repository reorganization — 2026-09-24

Owner approved the six integration repositories, minimal/Kajenn reorganization
and native Django alignment (constitution 11.19–11.20). Implementation is local:
minimal owns the unchanged generic ASGI adapter plus browser/Worker packaging;
Kajenn imports minimal and exposes its host integration; Django uses ordinary
views/URLconf with the neutral core Host. Hello World has five Python host profiles
and uses the new local package names. The original core 0.1.0 assets are unchanged.

Verified locally: installed minimal ASGI protocol with Kajenn imports blocked;
exporter 3/3 and installed CLI/Chromium file-origin live Source/Worker without
HTTP(S); Kajenn native checks 2/2, Ruff, strict Sphinx, wheel imports and sdist
mirror contents; Hello World Python/JS checks and all five installed Python profile
imports; Django installed page/asset and Chromium heading/disposal smoke. Django native tests pass 3/3, covering lifecycle/ownership, request rejection,
capacity and application error mapping; Ruff, strict docs and package builds pass.
Its local CI configuration now builds core browser assets before installation
and checks the installed native wheel; it has not been executed remotely. Core strict Sphinx
and public link/search/mirror checks pass. This is targeted integration evidence,
not a newly rerun full eight-profile browser matrix.

The owner deferred all integration GitHub publication until further reviewed PoC
transfer/cleanup (constitution 11.21), superseding the earlier Django publication
instruction. No push, remote rename, tag, release, registry publication or deployment
was performed. Physical repository paths and GitHub names remain unchanged; minimal
and Kajenn are local development package identities. Future Kajenn CI needs the
minimal source to be published; it is not remotely verified in this local phase.

Next phase, requiring owner-selected scope: review the remaining PoC transfers and
cleanup. Historical modules are evidence, not approved core capabilities. Publication
requires a new explicit owner instruction after those steps.

Owner-requested reminder: [GC-140](140-integrations-and-examples.md) records the
six integration repositories, the agreed Hello World application and its eight
execution profiles, plus publication and historical-example boundaries. No further
PoC transfer list has been agreed. This is documentation only; runtime and
verification results above are unchanged.

> **2026-09-25 supersession note:** The observed legacy null/attribute skip below is historical; 0.2.0 R1 preserves

Owner requests checking the legacy parameters before proceeding. Inspected
Genropy gnrpy/gnr/web/gnrwebstruct/base.py:data (line 793), matching the older
sourcerer clone gnrwebstruct.py:data (line 872), and browser genro_src.js:moveData
(line 602). The Python signature is data(self, *args, **kwargs). Two positional
arguments supply path/value; one argument without kwargs supplies value with no
explicit path; one with kwargs supplies path and null value. No positional
arguments leaves path/value null. dict values become Bags. The emitted Source
has tag data, attribute path, and the value as child content, not as a value
attribute. Other kwargs are carried as attributes. serverpath/_serverpath are
special: server context registration and canonical serverpath in Source.

Browser moveData resolves path through SourceNode. It writes only if the Data
node is absent or the declared value is non-null. Thus explicit null does not
overwrite an existing value, unlike the inspected PoC setter. It consumes
serverpath and shared_id/shared_* for server/shared-object services; a truthy
remote routes to dataRemote rather than ordinary initialization. These are
legacy observations, not authorization to add server synchronization or services.

stubbed child/Page/Bag dependencies: argument dispatch, attributes, dict-to-Bag
construction and _serverpath handling. This is not a full legacy integration
run. Browser conditions were inspected, not browser-tested in this checkpoint.

### Chronological teaching structure — owner clarification, 2026-10-13

Release sequence is the primary learning structure. A recurring example is an
intentional comparison: retain its earlier stage and then show which code the new
feature replaces or eliminates, why, and whether the visible result is unchanged.
Do not silently modernize the earlier lesson into the later one. Prerequisite maps
and concept indexes support this sequence. Package versions have independent
numbering; name the core milestone separately from the example package's release.
Current catalogue entries are maintained pages, not frozen runnable snapshots.

This supersedes the earlier proposal to use a cross-release concept route as the
primary order. D3 labels and preserves the stages; D4 places each gap at the release
where its feature entered; D5 returns to the same complete page in later stages;
D6 checks the before/after claims as well as the final result. No runtime or gallery
schema change, new example key or additional phase is authorized by this clarification.

**Proposed teaching standard:** each example has an objective/prerequisites,
environment/opening instructions and initial state, Python-first code explanation
with equivalent JS and execution location, guided action/expected result/reason,
a small prediction or modification exercise with its answer, a likely mistake,
limitations/reference/next lesson. Explain new terms; one new idea in basic
lessons, composed ideas in advanced ones. UI labels describe actual measurements.
Separate advanced timing/errors; no internal-guide prerequisites or application
instrumentation that conceals the framework.

**D1 — Coverage and learning path.** Map all 38 entries and supported author APIs
(GC-090/095/100, binding/server contracts, active adapter guides) to contract,
guide, objective, example/exercise, check, language/environment and gap disposition.
Statuses: covered, explanation incomplete, missing demonstration, environment-only,
deferred, blocked. Original concept map (now a secondary index): setup/first page → HTML/SVG → Data/paths →
controls → formulas/controllers/Logic → events/lifecycle → RPC/errors → remote
Source → Data resolvers/cache → complete page. Essential path plus advanced
material; one Python setup first (proposed Uvicorn), other environments separately.
Preserve existing keys. Deliver matrix, prerequisite map and bounded revision/new
lesson list with destinations before D2–D5. Names follow GC-225/GE-010; missing
conventions require owner decision. Exit: every topic/example has a learning role
or explicit exclusion, no unresolved lesson scope or unsupported coverage claim.

**D2 — Guides.** Reconcile core orientation/GC-090/095, examples introductions and
active adapter writing/reference/troubleshooting guides; remote is no longer
future work, dataRemote does not imply all resolver features. Explain common
concepts centrally, link instead of duplicating contracts/suites. Preserve dated
text with Historical record banners and current pointers. Take phase 5 editorial
items (§015, §695 chronology, GC-230 planned/delivered Kajenn), using dated
corrections where necessary. Paired docs/anchors preserved; current releases only
in README/badge, development cache fixes clearly separated from published behavior.
Exit: coherent setup → lesson → reference without internal-history prerequisites.

**D3 — Existing lessons.** Apply the teaching standard to all 38 explanations,
pages, family introductions and cross-links; preserve equivalent Python/JS and
show Python's Logic companion. Prioritize c09–c14. c13: label mounts correctly,
explain last-successful-mount name/TYTX-parameter identity, key-order limitation
and cancellation; verify skipped calls independently from _onRemote counts.
Advanced exercises: delayed A/B/A and Bag mutation. The originally proposed
name-change exercise is excluded by the owner decision in §755. c14: first read,
response, expiry then read (not automatic TTL refresh), zero/one-time cache,
reactive arguments, failures and supported cancellation/lifetime. Do not invent
callbacks/error UI or reuse dataRpc-only callbacks. Exit: guided trial/self-check
per page, accurate explanation; exposed runtime defects block affected exercises.

**D4 — Missing coverage.** Follow D1, extending existing lessons or adding focused
ones: _userChanges exact-path versus container/child writes (programmatic exact-path
writes also trigger); named connect_on/context requires dotted resource groups and
an external resource-host lesson, not the common gallery (D1 corrections, §740);
_onBuilt versus _onStart/order/cleanup; #ANCHOR versus relative paths; inout typed
save/restore/export and other supported operations with local fixtures or explicit
manual checks, no real email/external-service effects. Auth: default refusal,
Source omission versus browser visibility; authenticated allow/deny only through
an existing environment identity integration, no new login system. Common resource
lessons use Page.css/same-name CSS/Logic; named requires/groups need genro-kajenn,
not the kajenn adapter or FileServer. Work outside the four Gramlot repositories
requires separate authorization. Exit: supported common gaps demonstrated and
checked; environment-specific/blocked/deferred items have destination/status/next
action for owner review. A limitation note does not count as a working example.

**D5 — Complete page.** Retain the earlier local-only stage, then revisit the
same page in later release stages, showing the code replaced by each new feature. Prefer extending an existing complete/end-to-end lesson:
initial Data, editing, computed value, action, server response, error. Related
variations explain choosing dataRpc/remote/dataRemote without forcing all into one
large page. A learner changes a requirement using previous lessons and checks the
result. Only approved Source/Bags/bindings/controllers/server APIs, no hidden
helpers or parallel state. Exit: equivalent Python/JS, no unexplained prerequisite.

**D6 — Qualification and editorial walkthrough.** Establish installed core/examples
state, refresh first-party dependencies at setup/update without pins/source-copy
edits. Run all current catalogue entries (including c09–c14 and additions) with
Python/JS tests and Chromium; derive expected entries from catalogue, detect skips,
assert behavior. Verify gallery delivery on Node/Bun, five Python adapters and
Worker/static export for supported scope. Record per-environment commands, entries,
outcomes and exclusions; check changed setup instructions in a clean local setup.
Examples checks stay downstream, never core-to-examples dependencies. Deterministic
race tests plus browser checks; local file/download/mail verification and manual
limits recorded. Required repo documentation/build checks, paired anchors/links,
package assets when changed. Independently walk reader instructions from setup to
complete page: rendering, source visibility, prerequisites, results, mistakes,
links; correct and recheck. Agent review is not novice-user evidence. Present
beginner, cache/remote and complete-page lessons for owner's didactic review.
Exit: contradictions closed, no unexplained gap, checks accounted for; blocked or
unavailable items explicitly disposed of, teaching acceptance separate from tests.

**Boundaries:** core guides/contracts; examples repo common pages/READMEs/catalogue/
gallery; Python/JS server repos environment setup/examples/checks. No runtime,
dependency-source, authentication/resource system, gallery component, release,
deployment or external-service action authorized. Style/class: teach agreed
string/null, report pending phase 4 parity; no coercion or false fix claim.
Q1/Q2 empty-name/direct Source changes stay undecided. Development corrections
are not published releases. Record implemented/verified/blocked/accepted after
each authorized step. D6 acceptance precedes separate phase 4 authorization;
phase 5 retains responsibility/Q1/Q2 and phase 6 final technical qualification
with affected teaching rechecks. GC-110 not reopened.

**Next action:** D1–D3 implemented and locally verified (§740–750). The owner
excluded variable remote methods (§755); there is no blocked name exercise to
complete. Ask to start D4; D5/D6, owner acceptance and stabilization phase 4 remain
pending. Track the unsupported runtime/test behavior separately as a technical
nonconformity, not an authoring extension.

uses an independent Gramlot instance, Source, Data and named logic within Shadow

APIs and shows trees, cached values and attributes. Selection and collapsed state
follow node identities. Inspection performs no target writes or resolver execution.
Closing/retargeting releases subscriptions; disconnect disposes the UI. The core
has no import or dependency on the tool. The Chrome extension and all dependencies
remain unmodified. Contract and setup: [GC-195](195-tools-inspector.md#gc-195-005).

visually inspected. These checks use the worktree's current core; they do not
qualify local changes in the coordinating checkout or claim a full core regression.

<a id="gc-070-820"></a>
## 820 · Phase 5 — Responsibility review and scoped deferral — 2026-10-14

Block ID: **GC-070-820**.

**Authority and scope.** The owner instructed "allora lascia stare questo punto
e prcedi col resto", after declining the common-attribute Builder extension and
stating that documenting the unsupported dynamic remote method is enough for now.
Constitution 11.66 records the deferral of additional enforcement/CustomTypes
integration. Existing helpers and runtime behavior are unchanged; a dynamic
method is not thereby supported. Q2 (live Source declaration edits) remains an
open contract decision: this review adds no trigger or lifecycle semantics.

### Request ownership

| Owner | Lifetime and effect | Cancellation and completion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SourceHandler.remoteSource` | One replacement per mounted target NodeBinding; validates incoming Source before replacing children | Superseding requests and node removal abort; request identity, signal, page state and binding state guard the mount; `finally` releases tracking and deletes only the matching map entry |
| `RemoteBinding` | Declarative parameters, condition, last successfully mounted cache and callback | Delegates transport/mount to SourceHandler; a false condition or cache hit cancels the pending request; failure does not overwrite the last successful cache |
| `Provider` for `dataRpc` | One triggered endpoint call per provider, optional result-path write and callbacks | Latest call wins; removal aborts; timeout races the call even if transport ignores its signal; superseded/closed calls cannot write or invoke completion callbacks |
| `Provider` for `dataRemote` and `RpcResolver` | Provider installs/replaces the resolver; resolver loads on reads, coalesces pending reads and applies cacheTime | Uninstall aborts its load and removes only the resolver it owns; resolver checks the signal even after an answer arrives; failure leaves the last value unchanged |
| `RpcHandler.call` | Shared envelope, request identity and typed response/error decoding | Passes the owner's signal to the transport; does not choose the owner's lifetime or Data/Source effect |

The shared invariants are ownership of the result, suppression of late answers,
cleanup on node removal and preservation of the last valid contents on failure.
Timers, callbacks, Source replacement and lazy Data loading have different
contracts. Similar AbortController/finally code is not evidence that one generic
request manager would be simpler. **Review conclusion:** no extraction or Provider
hierarchy rewrite is warranted by the inspected paths; none was implemented.
A false `dataRpc` condition only suppresses that invocation, whereas declarative
`remote` explicitly cancels in-flight work and `dataRemote` uninstalls its resolver.
Those different semantics must not be homogenized by a refactor.

### Provider and attribute ownership

| Declaration/table | Authoritative purpose | Review disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python `collections/binding.json`, packaged JS `builder/binding.json` | Five data elements and their signatures; `data_element` metadata | Byte-identical; `dataSetter` installs values, the other four have providers |
| `BindingRuntime.PROVIDERS` | Four concrete provider dispatch targets | Matches the grammar's executable providers; excluding dataSetter is intentional |
| `installation.js` provider/lifecycle/RPC lists | Received-Source placement rules; lifecycle restrictions; callbacks only on dataRpc | Same four provider tags; dataRemote intentionally has no startup lifecycle trigger |
| `providers.js` control attributes | Exclude control fields from endpoint/body arguments | Execution contract, not the HTML filtering list; includes resolved `if`/`else`, method, timeout and cacheTime |
| `source.js` code-attribute lists | Activate only declared inline code on received Source | Formula/controller bodies, RPC callbacks and remote controls have distinct roles; this is not a provider dispatch registry |
| Python/JS builder Data-path/inline maps | P18 path restrictions and mutually exclusive inline/named bodies | Corresponding mappings agree; no new grammar metadata is needed |
| Python/JS renderer binding filters | Keep runtime-only attributes out of DOM output | Matching names/prefixes; provider-only controls need not become universal HTML filters because provider nodes do not render |

No conflicting provider enumeration was found in these inspected paths. The
lists overlap because they answer different questions; replacing them with a
single new registry is not justified. Existing behavioral tests remain the parity
checks, rather than tests that merely copy the implementation's constants.

### Documentation, verification and next gate

The earlier editorial work already marks §015's S00 instructions historical,
corrects §695's chronology and distinguishes delivered Kajenn avatar auth from
planned genro-routes integration in GC-230. Public GC-095 and its mirror now
explicitly distinguish helper rejection from incomplete direct/edited Source
validation; no universal rejection is claimed.

**167 targeted JavaScript tests pass**, covering RPC, remote, dataRemote,
Source pipeline, providers, installation, inline code, authoring and lifecycle.
The first invocation used the system Python and failed subprocess imports; rerun

### Corrections exposed by qualification

- **Multiple-select initialization:** b09 put `topics: ['html']` inside the
  initial record. Recursive Bag population correctly made it a nested Bag,
  while a multiple select requires an array. Both Python and JS examples now

  the distinction; regression checks cover initial selection and editing.

  an untyped object/array. Using it in Restore therefore accepted a JSON export
  and replaced the target with the wrong logical structure. InOut now decodes
  with TYTX and requires a Bag root before writing Data, preserving the existing
  Save/Restore contract. Tests reject malformed JSON, plain objects, arrays,
  null/scalars and Bag JSON exports, retaining the original branch identity;
  typed date/datetime/decimal round trips still pass. GC-095 and its mirror
  state the boundary. No dependency source or permissive alternate path added.
- **Verification harnesses:** the Python page-browser check now supplies the
  existing fixture folder and calls its registered `check_fragment`; the
  Node/Bun gallery check uses IndexPage's current logo/color selectors. These
  correct stale test references, not application behavior.

then passed on that state; C07 verifies all four readable/minified artifacts.

Owner-approved scope: Source hover/focus +/−, a child-insertion dialog, branch drag and Undo/Redo. Implemented in the shared optional inspector and target-side agent. ## 1365. Adversarial review of containers and gallery integration — 2026-10-18

Owner asks for a thorough review of recent work for duplication, inconsistent
behavior, arbitrary constants and adherence to Gramlot's architecture. This is
an analysis phase: no implementation fixes, new API decisions, release or
publication are approved by this entry. Prior verification remains historical
evidence; it does not cover the reproduced gaps below.

Scope: border/drawer and selected containers; parent/renderer integration;
Python gallery composition, mobile presentation, guided lesson and layout
examples; connected themes/popup changes; the new inspector structural history
and its interaction with containers. JavaScript/serverless gallery qualification
remains deferred by the owner. The inspector's entire pre-existing feature set
was not requalified in this review.

### Reproduced findings

- **R01 / P1 — Inspector insertion leaves invalid container Source.**
  `InspectorHistory.insert()` invokes the Builder with empty attributes
  (`tools/gramlot-tools-inspector/src/inspector-history.js`, insert).
  Inserting contentPane into a borderContainer throws
  `Invalid border region: undefined`, but the Source child count increases
  from 1 to 2 and the inserted child has no region. Undo recovers it.
  Parent-specific required metadata must be collected/validated before the
  mutation; inventing an implicit region is not an approved solution. The
  generic HTML topology tests do not exercise this component constraint.
- **R02 / P2 — Tab keyboard order diverges from Source/display order.**
  `selected-container.js`, renderTabs keydown handler, iterates the insertion
  order of `#tabs`; moving existing entries in the DOM does not reorder that Map.
  Reproduction: Source.move(2, 0) changes visible order from Alpha/Beta/Gamma to
  Gamma/Alpha/Beta, but Home still selects Alpha. Navigation must use the same
  current ordered records as rendering. This matters with the newly supported
  inspector branch reordering.
- **R03 / P2 — Drawer background and automatic foreground have different
  sources.** `border-container.js` computes contrast from --drawer-background,
  while drawer_background is projected as an inline background property.
  On the Python l04 page, drawer_background='#eeeeee' produces background
  rgb(238,238,238) with white text. Both authoring paths must feed the same
  effective color before deriving contrast; an explicit foreground still wins.
- **R04 / P2 — Font customization can clip drawer captions.** The minimized
  reveal cross-axis default is capped at 20px independently of the font/padding.
  On Python l04, the default 11px font fits (17px client/scroll width), but
  --gramlot-drawer-font-size:18px gives 20px client width and 23px scroll width.
  Default geometry should derive from content/font/padding; explicit maximums
  may remain opt-in constraints. Requiring a theme to coordinate several
  independent tokens is not the automatic behavior the owner requested.
- **R05 / P2 — Guided review and execution share one cursor.** Back calls show()
  and changes position; resumed automatic advancement reads position+1 and can
  execute an already-applied action again. Reproduction: Next twice, Back,
  edit the target value, Resume, advance the timer: the edit is overwritten by
  the already-executed second step. The existing test checks only immediately
  after Resume and pauses before that timer. Review-only navigation needs a
  distinct execution cursor or a clearly confirmed replay contract; do not
  silently interpret review as replay.

### Structural cleanup findings (not additional proven runtime failures)

- **R06 — The gallery conversion is incomplete.** Example/Explanation uses
  tabContainer, but open-page tabs in page.py/index-page-runtime and source-file
  tabs in gallery.js still maintain their own selection, keyboard and hiding
  loops. Mobile keeps a separate Bag and restores some preferences by reading
  rendered data-* attributes. These are existing services reused during the
  approved transition, not evidence that example business Data are duplicated;
  nevertheless the gallery is not yet the fully declarative reference that the
  new components should make possible. Consolidate state ownership and migrate
  the remaining tab behavior instead of extending these parallel loops.
- **R07 — Parent component responsibilities leak into generic renderer code.**
  html.js, gramlot-renderer.js and Python/JS attribute filtering each name tab /
  stack / border tags explicitly. Parent metadata projection, callbacks and
  selection writes should converge on one reviewed component contract rather
  than requiring another set of renderer branches for every new container.
  This is a proposed architecture cleanup, not authorization to invent a new
  generic plugin/proxy API during a bug fix.
- **R08 — Presentation and qualification need consolidation.** Drawer CSS
  retains overridden labelled-handle width/height/padding rules alongside the
  newer unified-content rules. Gallery CSS retains selectors for the old shell
  alongside its container composition. Breakpoint 1023 appears in both JS and
  CSS; drawer icon gap and some tab geometry are fixed values. Audit active
  selectors, centralize semantic defaults and keep theme-sensitive dimensions
  derivable. Several new browser/history tests are densely compressed, which
  makes missing transitions and combinations harder to notice. Rewrite their
  setup/actions/assertions clearly and cover the five reproductions above.

### Parameterization assessment

Existing good choices: shared SelectedContainer for tab/stack semantics; stable
slotted panels; Source-owned structural closing; existing publish/subscribe;
Python examples using bindings and dataControllers; shared popup positioning;
CSS theme tokens; gallery-owned tutorial sequencing as explicitly authorized.
DOM creation inside a web component is its implementation responsibility, not an
application workaround. Observer/timer/drag handles are legitimate lifecycle
state, not duplicated application Data.

Do not turn every number into an authoring parameter. Demo sizes, slider bounds,
350ms carousel delay and per-step seconds already belong to the authored lesson.
Theme colors, spacing, typography and interaction presentation need coherent
semantic variables and useful derived defaults. The first guided lesson's l04
association and named controls are acceptable within its expressly bounded
scope; before extending to other lessons, move lesson identity, paths and voice
language into one lesson configuration rather than copying conditionals. Do not
create a general replay engine without a separate approved design.

### Verification and next step

Read-only qualification reran 13 core border/selection tests, 4 guided-player
unit tests and 7 inspector-history tests: **24 passed**. Additional temporary
probes reproduced R01, R02 and R05 using the actual Source/Bag/runtime/player;
Chromium against the Python gallery reproduced R03/R04. Reloading the example
iframe correctly stopped the guide and restored availability; that suspected
lifecycle defect was rejected. These checks are not a claim of complete suite
or audible narration qualification. No Node/serverless gallery was exercised.

Review complete. Fixes remain pending owner instruction. Recommended order:
R01-R05 regressions and repairs, then the bounded R06-R08 consolidation with any
new component-interface decision reviewed before implementation. Retain Python
preview-only verification until the owner accepts the final release phase.

<a id="gc-070-1450"></a>
## 1450. One request race, shared ids and topics, instance state; `Logic` optional (review p3) — 2026-10-19

Phase p3 of the review of the 0.3.5 releases. Implemented on the review branch; no
release or deployment is authorized.

- Requests: `RpcHandler.call` is the one cancellation of a call. Its `signal` and the
  dispose of the page (`gramlot.abort`) abort it; it then rejects at once with the
  abort reason, also when the transport does not stop on its signal; a call aborted
  before it starts is not sent. `remoteRequests` holds the AbortController of each
  call in flight by envelope id and is written only by `call`. `NodeBinding.call`
  sends the request of a node (`node.requests`) through it and the close of the node
  aborts it: used by `dataRpc`, `dataRemote` and `remoteSource`. A dispose during
  `main` rejects `start()` at once with "Gramlot was disposed during main".
- One random id helper, `randomId()` (`js/src/random-id.js`), for the RPC envelope,
  the frame session, the renderer instance, the Data subscription, the `__ref`
  reference and the ask dialogs.
- One topic loop, `SubscriptionsHandler.subscribeNode`, for providers (presence rule)
  and rendered nodes (handler required), both documented in GC-095 §115; every
  callback is asked before any subscription is made.
- `DATA_ROOT` is imported from `@genrojs/builders`. The TYTX `getDateType` copy in
  `format.js` stays, pointing to genro-org/genro-tytx#62.
- Instance state: `AskDialog` is one instance per page (`BindingRuntime.askDialog`);
  the panel and region configurations of the selection and border containers are
  static private fields of the component classes made per window by
  `ComponentCollection.register`. `window.gramlot` stays: GC-090 documents it.
- `_subscriptions` is read only by `Gramlot`; the binding runtime receives it at
  construction (`BindingRuntime.subscriptions`). `RpcResolver` writes through the
  public `node` of BagResolver; `_lastUpdate` stays, BagResolver has no public member
  for a load made outside `resolve`.
- `HttpTransport.close` keeps no empty `try/catch` and no `.catch(() => {})`.
- Decision d-logic (constitution 11.86): `Logic` is optional in a logic module; a
  module without it has no logic methods (GC-095 §060, GC-090 §030).

Verification: 3,598 JavaScript tests pass (baseline 3,593); Python 184 tests and 323
subtests pass with the existing expected failure. Chromium checks pass: binding,
messaging, border, page module, components, runtime, component review. Docs:
`prepare_docs`, Sphinx `-W` and `check_public_docs.py` pass.

<a id="gc-070-1475"></a>
## 1475. Page expiry renewed by use; version-free exclusion messages; unique document ID (review p4c) — 2026-10-19

Phase p4c of the review of the 0.3.5 releases (owner decision 2026-10-19: a page expires
`page_ttl` seconds after its last use, not after it was opened). Implemented on the review
branch; no release or deployment is authorized.

- Page expiry, Python and JavaScript (GC-230 §010, GC-101 §010): `GramlotServer` sets the
  expiry of a page to now plus `page_ttl`/`pageTtl` when the page is opened and again for
  every call that names a page of its owner that has not expired, whatever the outcome of
  the method (`not_found`, `not_authenticated`, `not_authorized` and `application_error`
  included). One private method computes it (`_expiry`, JS `#expiry`; GC-225 §025). Until
  now a page expired 1800 seconds after it was opened even while in use. A call of another
  owner, of an unknown or of an expired page, a request that cannot be decoded and the close
  message renew nothing. The renewal is in `GramlotServer.call`: adapters do nothing for it
  and must not read the registry (`_pages`, `pages`).
- Owner cookie (GC-230 §135, GC-101 §135): it has no lifetime today (`Path`, `HttpOnly`,
  `SameSite=Lax`, no `Max-Age`, no `Expires`). It is a session cookie that nothing renews, so
  the core API gives no value to re-issue; documented, and kept without lifetime. The expiry
  of a page does not depend on it.
- Tests with a clock the test moves, no waiting: Python `PageExpiryTests`
  (`tests/test_source_server.py`) replaces `time` in the server module; JavaScript `page expiry`
  tests (`js/tests/gramlot-server.test.js`) replace `performance.now`. They cover the call
  after half the TTL, the page idle for longer than the TTL, the page never called, every
  outcome of an accepted call, the calls that are not accepted and the page a call does not
  name.
- Conformance (GC-230 §150 item 18), Python and JavaScript: `check_protocol(..., page_ttl=)`
  and `checkProtocol(..., {pageTtl})` take the short TTL of the adapter's server and check
  a call at 0.5 TTL, a call at 1.2 TTL after the opening (renewed by the first) and
  `page_expired` 1.3 TTL after the last call, about 2.5 TTL in all; without the argument
  the item is left out, so released adapters are not affected. The reference adapters take
  the TTL (`tests/http_server.py --page-ttl`, `pageTtl` of `startServers`); the core tests
  run both checks against the reference adapters at 0.8 seconds, and against an adapter whose TTL
  is not the one given.
- Messages "excluded from Gramlot 0.2.0" are "excluded from Gramlot": `builder.py`,
  `gramlot-builder.js` and the `PUBLISH` macro of `inline.js`; their tests match the end of
  the message.
- Document ID GC-105 was used twice. The internal register of Python and JavaScript Builder
  differences is GC-106 (`docs/internal/106-builder-python-js-differences.md`, anchors
  `gc-106-NNN`); GC-005 §010 item 4 records it and the links of the READMEs, GC-125 and
  PORT-0004 name the new file. The public guide Components keeps GC-105.
- Docs: GC-230 §010, §025, §135, §150, GC-101 §010, §025, §135 and the conformance list,
  GC-090 §020, GC-225 §025, GC-005, with their docs_llm mirrors.

Verification: 3,643 JavaScript tests pass (baseline 3,635); Python 212 tests and 369
subtests pass with the existing expected failure (baseline 204 and 365). Docs: `prepare_docs`,

## 1480. Theme serving on GramlotServer; IndexPage without the base theme (review p4d) — 2026-10-19

Phase p4d of the review of the 0.3.5 releases (two follow-ups found by the js-server phase).
Implemented on the review branch; no release or deployment is authorized.

- `theme_file`/`themeFile` (GC-230 §145, GC-101 §145) moves from `GramlotFileServer` to
  `GramlotServer`, Python and JavaScript; `GramlotFileServer` inherits it and the public names
  do not change. The method does not read the pages folder, and the bootstrap of every page lists
  the base theme, so a `GramlotServer` that resolves its pages another way listed a theme it did
  not serve. `theme_css`/`themeCss` was already on `GramlotServer`.
- The file lookup is in a new module, `files.py`/`files.js` (`file_below`/`fileBelow`, `THEMES`;
  JavaScript also `inside` and `realFile`); `companion_file`/`companionFile` uses it too. GC-225
  gets the row "Helper modules" (the module `files` is a provisional implementation, not an
  accepted name or design; see §1483).
- JavaScript: `gramlot-server.js` is the neutral module that the serverless Worker bundles for the
  browser, so it cannot import Node.js: esbuild stops at `node:fs/promises`, a literal
  `import()` included. `themeFile` loads `files.js` on its first call with `import(NODE_FILES)`,
  a constant specifier that the bundler leaves alone. A Worker has no files and never calls it.
  A test builds `gramlot-server.js` for the browser and fails on a Node.js import. A JSR
  publication may report the dynamic import as not analysable (a warning to check at the next
  publication).
- `IndexPage.css` (Python and JavaScript) is `/themes/gramlot-index/theme.css`; the base theme
  comes from the server (`css_theme`/`cssTheme`, GC-230 §010). A server with `css_theme=False`
  no longer loads Base for the index shell. Nothing in the core reads `css[0]`.
- Adapters: js-server `server/src/fetch.mjs` serves themes only when
  `server instanceof GramlotFileServer`; the condition applies to the companion files alone.
  py-server `base.py` already calls `server.theme_file`; its `server_class` stays
  `GramlotFileServer` while the base takes a pages folder.
- Docs: GC-101 §005 and §145, GC-230 §005 and §145, GC-090 §017 and §020, GC-096 §045,
  GC-225 §010 and item 1 of the constitution amendment of the review, with their docs_llm
  mirrors.

## 1481. Typed literals in JavaScript page modules, `dataRemote` cache, theme classes `actions` and `eyebrow` (review p4e) — 2026-10-19

Phase p4e of the review of the 0.3.5 releases (defects found by the examples phase).
Implemented on the review branch; no release or deployment is authorized.

- Typed literals (GC-090 §024, GC-097 §045). The server runs `main` of a JavaScript page
  module and the browser imports the same module for its `Logic`. In the browser the import
  map resolves only `@gramlot/gramlot/page`. The runtime, which that name meant in the browser,
  exported `Bag` and `BagNode` but not `createDecimal`; `src/server/page.js`, which it meant on
  the server, exported none of the three. A module that imported them did not load in one context
  or the other, and the examples w10 and w20 had dropped the literals their Python twins keep.
  `src/server/page.js` and the runtime
  (`src/index.js`) now export `Bag`, `BagNode` and `createDecimal`, with the names of the Bag and
  TYTX libraries and no alias. A date or a time is a `Date`, typed by TYTX from its content
  (midnight UTC `D`, the epoch day `H`, any other instant `DHZ`): it needs no export.
  `isDecimal` is not exported: it is not an authoring need. Python needs no change: its pages
  import `Decimal`, `datetime` and `Bag` from their packages. GC-225 gets the row "Typed literals
  of the page entry" (confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-20).
- Tests. `js/tests/page-literals.test.js` (4 tests) and the fixture `js/tests/fixtures/page-literals/`:
  the page entry of the server and the runtime export the same page surface; one page module
  builds a Decimal, a date, a date and time, a time and a Bag, once with the name resolved by
  Node to `src/server/page.js` and once, in a child process, with a resolve hook that maps it to
  `dist/gramlot.js` as the import map does; both give the same TYTX text. The Python twin is
  `test_typed_literals_have_the_wire_types_of_the_javascript_page` in `tests/test_source_server.py`.
  `scripts/verify_page_module_browser.mjs` now authors a Decimal literal in the page (JavaScript and
  Python) and passes on Chromium for the four page forms. The JavaScript Decimal travels as `12.5::N`
  for `createDecimal('12.50')`: the Decimal library of the JavaScript TYTX does not keep the trailing
  zero that Python writes (`12.50::N`); the value is the same.
- `dataRemote` cache (`js/src/binding/rpc-resolver.js`). The asynchronous load recorded the cache
  time but not the fingerprint of the parameters that `BagResolver.resolve` records, so the first
  explicit read after a changed `^` argument, which installs a new resolver that loads at once, found
  another fingerprint and made one more synchronous call (3 requests instead of 2 in the example c14).
  `#load` now takes the fingerprint at the start of the load, as `resolve` does before its load, and
  records it with the cache time when the answer is written; a load that is ignored, aborted or
  of a closed node records nothing. The test `sync: the asynchronous load of a changed ^ param
  records the parameters: the first explicit read makes no call` counts 1 synchronous and 1 asynchronous
  request. GC-099 §105 states it.
- Theme (GC-096 §035). `gramlot-base` had no class for a row of actions or for the small label
  above a heading; five lesson stylesheets of `gramlot-examples` copied `.actions` and four copied
  `.eyebrow`. The layer `gramlot.utilities` now has `.actions` (`display: flex`, wrapping, gap

  stylesheets keep their copies until `gramlot-examples` removes them; they are unlayered and win.

<a id="gc-070-1482"></a>
## 1482. Style shortcuts take their CSS unit; a few legacy sub-keys read a number as pixels (review p13a, p13c) — 2026-10-20

Phases p13a and p13c of the review of the 0.3.5 releases (documentation fix, owner decisions of
2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20).
Implemented on the review branch; no release or deployment is authorized.

- Rule (GC-096 §040). The value of a style shortcut is written with its CSS unit, as in legacy
  GenroPy (`genro_dom.js` `getStyleDict` copies the value unchanged): `width="20px"`,
  `margin_top="4px"`. A number without a unit is not valid CSS: `width=20` is written as
  `width: 20` and the browser ignores the declaration (verified in the Python renderer). Properties
  whose CSS value is a plain number (`opacity`, `z_index`, `line_height`) take a number. SVG
  presentation attributes are not style shortcuts: `svg(width=100)` stays valid. The sub-keys that
  read a number as pixels are in the last bullet of this entry (p13c).
- Examples and sentences corrected: GC-095 §005 (`margin_top=4` is now `margin_top='4px'`, with a
  pointer to the rule) and GC-097 §070, block GC-095-070 (the sentence that numeric shortcuts such as `width=10` are
  accepted now says the value is not checked for a unit and points to the rule). The other public
  examples already carry units (`width="12rem"`, `width="^width:{}px"`). The regional dimensions of
  `borderContainer` (GC-105 §100) are a component contract, not a style shortcut, and keep their
  pixel numbers.
- Decided (owner, 2026-10-20, p13c). The finding of p13a is closed: a number becomes pixels only in
  the sub-keys inherited from the legacy, and GC-096 §040 lists them. The keys were verified in the
  source of the Builder renderers, not only in the bundle: `px()` of `@genrojs/builders`
  (`src/renderer/html.js`, `_macro_rounded`, `_macro_transform`, `_macro_filter`) and `_px()` of
  `genro_builders` (`contrib/html/html_renderer.py`, the same three methods). Both convert the
  same keys, checked by rendering each key in Python and in JavaScript with identical output:
  - `rounded` and its forms `rounded_top`, `rounded_bottom`, `rounded_left`, `rounded_right`,
    `rounded_top_left`, `rounded_top_right`, `rounded_bottom_left`, `rounded_bottom_right`
    (legacy `css3style_rounded`, `v+'px'`);
  - `transform_translate_x` and `transform_translate_y` (legacy `css3style_transform`, lines 535-536
    of `genro_dom.js`);
  - `filter_blur`: the Builder renderers convert it, legacy `css3style_filter` has no `blur`
    (it reads `rotate`, `invert` and `contrast`).
  Only a number converts; a string is written as given (`rounded="4"` gives `4`). Gramlot has no
  code of its own for this: `GramlotHtmlRenderer.adaptAttrs`/`adapt_attrs` call the Builder renderer.
- Difference from legacy, not changed: legacy `css3style_shadow` adds `px` to `x`, `y` and `blur`
  and builds `box-shadow`. The Builder renderers write the parts of `shadow` as
  `box-shadow-<part>: <value>` (`shadow_x=2` gives `box-shadow-x: 2`, not a CSS property) and pass a
  full `shadow="…"` value through. GC-096 §040 says that `shadow` takes a complete `box-shadow` value.
  Python and JavaScript do not differ from each other. Correcting the renderers would be an issue in
  `genro-builders` and `genro-builders-js`.
- Docs: GC-095 §005, GC-096 §040, GC-097 §070 with their docs_llm mirrors.

Verification: 3,651 JavaScript tests pass (baseline 3,651); Python 215 tests and 382
subtests pass with the existing expected failure (baseline 215 and 382). Docs: `prepare_docs`,

  `genro-tytx>=0.16.3`, whose `to_tytx` writes compact JSON with or without orjson (genro-org/genro-tytx#60); the
  null-attribute probe asserts that output.

  (PyPI and npm).

  job now has `continue-on-error: true` and `timeout-minutes: 20` (#52, #53). The gallery updater ignores the `jsr`
  job of a completed publication run and keeps the npm and PyPI gates (gramlot-examples #23, #24, installed on the

External review of the published releases, three points, all confirmed and corrected on `develop`:

1. JSR package. `js/src/server/files.js` finds the themes at `../../themes/`, which is `js/themes/` in the npm
   package. `jsr.json` published `themes/**` at the package root, so the server of the JSR package found no theme.
   `jsr.json` now publishes `js/themes/**`, the copy made by the build, as npm does. `scripts/check_jsr_package.mjs`
   rebuilds the package from a `jsr publish --dry-run` file list and calls `GramlotServer.themeFile` on it: base and
   compact themes found, a missing file and paths outside the folder refused. The `jsr` job runs it before
   publishing. The published JSR 0.3.6 keeps the defect until the next core release.
2. WebKit binding check. `scripts/verify_binding_browser.mjs` focused the host of the button components `#bctrl` and
   `#bonly`; in WebKit the focus stayed on `BODY`. The script now focuses their inner `<button>` and asserts that it
   holds the focus before pressing Enter and Space. It passes in Chromium and WebKit, and the CI runs it in both.

[GC-197](197-legacy-tree.md) inventories the tree runtime, store, Dojo behavior,
wrapper families and IDE consumers. Its Python census found 90 direct declarations
in 1,649 files with no parse errors. A generic Bag tree is a bounded candidate;
IDE-like lazy navigation additionally requires adapting to the current core
resolver contract. PoC and core resolver reads differ. Checkbox propagation,
search, drag/drop, tree grids, relation/database and storage services have separate
proposed increments. A DOM-harness reproduction confirmed the PoC stale-selection
highlight defect after a redraw.

CKEditor, TinyMCE and Dojo Editor, including parameter precedence, dynamic changes,
callbacks, commands, compositions and GNRIde flows. Its Python census found 68
direct declarations in the same 1,649-file corpus with no parse errors. Each
capability distinguishes straightforward PoC recovery, adaptation, new port work
and owner decisions. A bounded CodeMirror field is the smallest candidate, but
requires explicit integration with current component binding/events/lifecycle.
HTML/Markdown representation and fidelity, configurable toolbars, diagnostics,
uploads, templates, PDF and IDE document services remain visible in the matrix.

and external applications are explicit completeness limits.

## 1535. FramePage / IndexPage inheritance — initial design direction, 2026-10-20

Block ID: **GC-070-1535**.

Owner proposed “potrtemmo avere un frame page con le 5 region eccetera e la index page avrebbe la navifgazioen e i pannelli del tab container”. After the explicit FramePage → IndexPage → gallery separation was restated, the owner confirmed “si inizialmente si poi verifichiamo”. This is an initial design direction to detail and verify, not final API acceptance or implementation authorization.

FramePage is a reusable Python/JS Page base offering top, bottom, left, right and center regions, region-content hooks and configuration of dimensions, splitters and drawers. IndexPage inherits that frame and adds navigation, tabContainer panels and selection coordination. The gallery specializes IndexPage with its example catalogue, code on the right, configuration below and title/Inspector above. The base must not depend on gallery-specific controls, IDs or Code/Navigation toolbar buttons. Applications may subclass either level and override the declared hooks.

Pending contract decisions: exact hook names/signatures, optional-region/default behavior, configuration and Data ownership, navigation/panel lifecycle and migration of existing IndexPage responsibilities. No new hook spelling, compatibility layer or framework implementation is approved by this record. The isolated optional-toolbar-button patch discussed in §1530 has not been approved; discussion now concerns the reusable page contract. Previously implemented toolbar Inspector and Settings drawer remain in place. Maximum-tab/LRU behavior remains unconfirmed. Next: detail the frame contract one decision at a time, then verify the agreed design. Documentation only; no runtime changes or tests in this step.


Owner confirmation of the first frame rule, 2026-10-20: “si procediamo svelti” answers the proposal “centro disponibile, quattro regioni esterne facoltative; una regione non definita non occupa spazio e non mostra drawer”. The center is available; top/bottom/left/right are optional, with no allocated space or drawer for an undefined region. This confirms that rule only; hook signatures, region-detection mechanism and implementation remain to be settled. Continue with a concrete compact hook proposal; do not reinterpret the request for speed as approval of unspecified APIs.


Owner confirmation of region hooks, 2026-10-20: “si” answers the concrete proposal `top(pane)`, `bottom(pane)`, `left(pane)`, `right(pane)`, `center(pane)`, with identical names in Python and JS. Each hook receives its region's contentPane, configures it and constructs its contents. An outer region is created only when its hook is defined, including an inherited implementation. IndexPage implements left for navigation and center for tabContainer; the gallery specializes right for code, bottom for Settings, top for title/Inspector. This settles hook spelling/signatures and the outer-region presence rule, superseding the corresponding open items above. Region configuration mechanics, Data ownership and navigation/panel lifecycle still need a concrete contract. No runtime changes in this step.


Owner confirmation of IndexPage navigation, 2026-10-20: “ok” answers the proposal to use the shared tree with a Bag store, including resolvers, as standard navigation. Selecting a navigation entry opens its corresponding tabContainer panel or reactivates that panel if already open. The derived page supplies the navigation Bag and defines panel construction. This confirms the base behavior, not a new node-metadata schema, tab-identity algorithm, construction-hook signature, asynchronous loading/error policy or maximum-tab eviction rule. Those details remain to be settled; no implementation in this documentation step.


Owner confirmation of panel construction, 2026-10-20: “ok” answers the proposal `panel(pane, node)`. The pane is the tab's content panel; node is the selected Bag navigation node. The derived page constructs Gramlot content there and may choose an iframe. The hook runs on first opening; selecting the same entry again reactivates its existing tab and preserves its state. This settles the conceptual hook contract and first-open reuse behavior, not the Python/server versus browser invocation mechanism or serialization of the selected node. Entry identity, navigable/category distinction, asynchronous failure/retry, disposal and tab-limit policy remain unresolved. No runtime implementation in this step.


Owner confirmation and filesystem navigation direction, 2026-10-20: “si oppure se preferisci puoi mettere un hash” confirms the proposed initial behavior: a navigation entry's URL identifies a page loaded in an iframe; selecting the same URL reactivates the same tab. Hash algorithm, URL equivalence/normalization and collision handling are not established by this confirmation.

The owner continues: “potremmo costrire l'albero a partire dal filesistem” with nested folders, each folder a resolver, and an intermediate folder potentially having “una info o meta o index” as its own direct page. Exact directory-page filename conventions, metadata schema, discovery/host ownership and implementation remain unresolved. Folder expansion and page navigation must be distinguished in the concrete contract; no filesystem access or new resolver implementation is claimed here. The previously confirmed panel(pane, node) hook remains a specialization point; the initial default is URL/iframe navigation, not arbitrary server execution of a browser BagNode.


Owner confirmation of directory-page convention, 2026-10-20: “si” answers the proposal to use `index.py` or `index.js`, according to the environment, as the directory's own page. This applies to intermediate directories as well as other directory nodes. The directory's children remain supplied through its resolver; its own index page is independently addressable by URL for iframe/tab navigation. This settles the filename convention only. The earlier info/meta alternatives are not adopted as alternate page-discovery names. No metadata-file contract, cross-language precedence, filesystem resolver implementation or host integration is approved or claimed by this documentation step.

In Builder Python `_split_annotated` extracts validators from a top-level Annotated or a single non-null Optional branch, but not from a bool-or-Annotated-string Union. `_check_type` visits Union branches, enforces custom-type/dtype metadata, then drops the remaining Annotated metadata; `_validate_call_args` receives no Regex validator for the Union. Each receives the relevant typed data and determines eligibility through true/false; these checks supplement dropTargetCb and any rejection vetoes the drop. They do not implicitly add accepted dropTypes. Invoke a typed eligibility callback only when its type is present in the drag. ## 1550. General drop action and target check implemented — 2026-10-20

Owner-approved general onDrop and dropTargetCb callback envelopes are implemented as separate renderer steps using existing named Logic invocation. invokeDrop receives {dropValues, item, path, source, selfdrop, dropEffect, dataAvailable}, skips empty residual data or an unavailable handler/destination, and awaits asynchronous application work. checkDropTarget receives the same envelope and requires a synchronous boolean. A missing dynamic callback adds no restriction; a detached destination rejects. Each call reads the current renderer record and application Data, rather than caching the eligibility result.

Both attributes remain runtime metadata in Python/JavaScript and do not become inline DOM event attributes. The source descriptor is passed through, without inventing its cross-window identity fields. These helpers do not perform the full drop pipeline: declarative type/tag/effect eligibility, native routing, typed dispatch, accepted-drop publishes, snapshot serialization and cleanup remain separate responsibilities. In particular, a successful checkDropTarget alone is not complete acceptance, and invokeDrop assumes already accepted data with typed-handled entries removed. No automatic Bag move/copy or DOM reparenting is introduced.

### Legacy capability inventory

| Area | Observed behavior and qualification |
| --- | --- |
| Title and content | Reactive title; arbitrary nested layout/content; inherited ContentPane loading is separate from application-specific helpers. Legacy setTitle uses innerHTML, which must not be transferred as an unsanitized title policy. |
| Movement | The inherited Dialog installs TimedMoveable on its title bar. Movement and modality already coexist. |
| Manual resizing | No built-in user resize grip was found in the reviewed Dialog path. Its resize method and automatic adaptation are not evidence of manual resizing. FloatingPane explicitly supports resizable and ResizeHandle. |
| Automatic dimensions | autoSize; viewport bounds with restoration of initial dimensions; windowRatio; parentRatio; fullScreen; descendant layout resizing. |
| Position | Default centering; centerOn and xRatio/yRatio; stacked dialogs offset from their parent. A position attribute appears in examples but is consumed in creating without a clear implementation in this reviewed path; do not promise it from those examples alone. |
| Closing | closable defaults false in the Gramlot-like Genro wrapper; true exposes ordinary cancellation, ask requests confirmation with close_msg/confirm/cancel/action, publish emits a close intent for application handling. show/hide retain the widget; higher-level quickDialog may destroy its temporary Source branch. |
| Nested dialogs | dialogStack, parent/child resize propagation, underlay/z-index and parent modal reconnection. |
| Keyboard and focus | Dojo provides focus capture, Tab boundaries, Escape and refocus. Genro's versionpatch_11__onKey deliberately replaces that keyboard handler with an empty implementation for CKEditor: upstream behavior must not be claimed as intact in the configured wrapper. |
| Nonmodal option | noModal is consumed only to choose a lower starting z-index in the reviewed wrapper; no complete alternate nonmodal interaction path was established. Use the floating-container evidence for nonmodal behavior. |
| Appearance and lifecycle | duration, animateResize appearance animation, onShowing/afterShow and window-resize connections. Legacy timing/global lifecycle mechanisms are evidence, not a destination implementation. |
| Floating windows | FloatingPane movement, optional resizeAxis x/y/xy, resize handle, bringToTop, show/hide, close removes Source, maximize/restore, minimize/dock. ResizeHandle supports live or outlined resizing, animation and minimum dimensions. |
| Geometry persistence | FloatingPane saves local geometry by page/nodeId, restores within parent bounds; persist=False and fixedPosition bypass restoration. Palette recipe defaults include resizable=True and docking/show controls. |
| Higher-level compositions | simpleDialog/formDialog/iframeDialog/confirm; alert/ask/prompt/askParameters; quickDialog/remoteDialog; iframe/lightbox/editor/upload/data-editor compositions. These are separate recipes/services with additional ownership and dependencies, not mandatory features of the base container. |

### Destination assessment and remaining decisions

The owner's movable/resizable/modal requirement is accepted. Proposed browser
foundation: native HTML dialog opened via showModal, with framework-owned title
dragging and resize handles; geometry changes must not close/reopen the dialog
or replace its children. The HTML standard defines document blocking and focus
handling for modal dialogs:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-dialog-element .
The modal scope is its document; blocking a containing page from inside an iframe
would require a separate host-level contract, not automatic cross-frame access.

Proposed base behavior for review: Python-declared title/content and geometry,
bound visibility, explicit movement/resizing controls, viewport bounds, reliable
focus and retained field drafts across close/reopen, plus nested modal qualification.
Floating remains the nonmodal counterpart; the PoC palette supplies behavior evidence.
Persistence, docking, maximize, fullscreen, proportional sizing, animation, lazy
content and confirmation recipes remain separately selectable; no blanket port
or omission is approved by this inventory.

First open behavior decision: ordinary user closing through X/Escape versus
an application-controlled close request that can refuse closure or ask confirmation.
Further decisions include public names/native dialog coexistence, bound open-state
name/defaults, retention and geometry persistence. New API names must be recorded
in GC-225 after confirmation. Reuse current Source/Data/Container ownership and
existing remote/ask services where their contracts apply; no Builder/Bag or legacy
source changes and no parallel modal stack or renderer are authorized by this review.

Verification is source inspection and cross-checking wrappers against inherited
Dojo behavior and Python examples. No legacy/browser runtime test was run and no
new dialog/floating implementation exists. Future focused browser regressions
must cover mouse and keyboard blocking during drag/resize, viewport resize, nested
dialog focus restoration, Escape/close policy, retained drafts, component removal,
pointer cancellation and no surviving listeners. This review does not re-run
release qualification or classify either future component as Alpha/Beta/Stable.

Owner answers "ok. poi vorrei che tu inventariassi anche frame pane e slotbar".

can be intercepted by the application to veto closing or request confirmation;
without interception, closing proceeds normally. It does not settle callback
names, asynchronous execution contracts or the rest of the dialog API.

### Availability and provenance

Neither framePane nor slotBar was found in the inspected core or PoC runtime,
Python authoring or collection metadata. Core also lacks slotToolbar/slotFooter.
Core has borderContainer/contentPane and the Python FramePage class. FramePage
is a whole-page five-region composition using overridable hooks; it does not
supply the legacy embeddable framePane API or named-slot bars.

Legacy reference: GenroPy@fa35e5adfa6ad1b269f3a22a9b12c4c1ee6513ea:
gnrpy/gnr/web/gnrwebstruct/base.py (__getattr__, framepane);
gnrpy/gnr/web/gnrwebstruct/dojo11.py (lines 677–783);
gnrjs/gnr_d11/js/genro_components.js (FramePane at 811, SlotBar at 6155);
projects/gnrcore/packages/test/webpages/layout/framepane.py.
PoC checked at 10478b57ce3f22e6445eb6b72eba343520cbebac.

### FramePane inventory

- Python authoring: framePane(frameCode, centerCb, **kwargs), automatic unique
  frameCode when omitted/templated, and lazy named top/bottom/left/right/center
  authoring slots through the legacy structure's attribute lookup.
- Rendering: composition into BorderContainer and ContentPane, headline/sidebar
  region ordering, propagation of frameCode, region splitters and side parameters.
- Center: explicit center content or a generated center pane configured through
  center_*; ordinary content is directed to the center by the runtime composition.
- Identity: registration as frameCode + "_frame", optional frameTarget identity,
  region child names and legacy _frame children.
- Presentation: redistribution of rounded-corner parameters to outer regions.
- Related FrameForm/store/record behavior is a separate composition; it is not
  intrinsic to FramePane and does not authorize database/form-service imports.

Existing borderContainer already owns layout, splitters, drawers, sizing and
retained children. A future framePane should reuse that responsibility rather
than implement another layout engine. Legacy automatic region access and center
routing require an explicit authoring contract; inspection does not establish
equivalent Builder capabilities or authorize dependency changes.

### SlotBar inventory

- Ordered comma-separated slot names; named Python access such as
  bar.save.button(...), with arbitrary Source children inside a slot.
- Layout tokens: "*" elastic space, "|" separator, numeric fixed pixel space.
  Horizontal and vertical implementations differ; vertical "*" only creates
  an empty row in the reviewed code, so equal elastic behavior is not proven.
- Orientation defaults from the containing region; explicit orientation supported.
  Slot-level width/height/alignment and table_*, row_*, cell_*, lbl_* presentation.
- Labels: horizontal label positions N/T/B/L/R and per-item label parameters;
  vertical implementation does not provide equivalent label layout.
- Python recipe lookup by frame/slotbar prefix, optional namespace and generic
  slotbar_<name>; slot@parameter syntax and per-slot prefixed arguments.
- slotbar_updateslotsattr rebuilds authored slots; slotbar_replaceslots supports
  replacement/insertion with "#" referring to the prior list. These are Python
  construction helpers, not evidence of general reactive browser reordering.
- slotToolbar and slotFooter are presentation helpers over slotBar; slotButton
  is a related icon/tooltip button surface, not the bar itself.
- Built-in JavaScript slot builders: searchOn, pageBranchSelector, stackButtons,
  parentStackButtons, fieldsTree, count, messageBox and dashboardSaver. They carry
  additional search, page-shell, database, messaging or dashboard dependencies.
- Frame integration includes side styling, slotbar identity and closable handles.

Proposed bounded future scope: named slots, ordering, spacers/separators,
orientation, ordinary Gramlot children and Python composition. Legacy method
fallback chains, global frame lookup, table-based rendering, unsanitized innerHTML,
and application-specific built-in slots are not automatically part of the port.
This proposal and final API/implementation ownership remain unapproved. Keep
availability distinct from Alpha/Beta/Stable maturity; no level is assigned here.

generated payload; evt is included. A supplied action overrides publish generation.

## 1930 · Gallery page-loading diagnosis — 2026-10-24

Owner asks to investigate slow page loading. Read-only runtime diagnosis on the
Python gallery at localhost:8098, Chromium, fresh browser context: shell ready
in 1.817 s; textbox first opening 4.614 s; Mela first opening 2.900 s; returning
to the already-open textbox 41 ms with no requests. These are local observations,
not release benchmarks; the first click overlapped the introduction iframe load.

Confirmed causes:
- Gallery supplies inputs, layout, tree, editors and typst as server-wide
  collections. Every example iframe receives all five, including the 42,749,653
  byte Typst JS bundle and 4,686,602 byte editor bundle.
- The running Python adapter sends collection assets with Cache-Control: no-store.
  New frames request the large bundles again; existing example tabs retain state.
- Core open_page verifies selected artifacts; each Source request verifies them
  again and calls load_collection separately. Gramlot's grammar composition
  copies and reparses the accumulated grammar on each load. Profiling the textbox
  Source call attributed about 93–95% of instrumented time to load_collection.
  Uninstrumented five-run median: all five collections 887 ms; only inputs and
  layout 176 ms, both producing 24,108-character Source responses. The attempted
  inputs-only control failed correctly because formlet belongs to layout.
- Adapter resource URL lookup and asset serving also call artifact verification.
  Isolated median verification cost was about 48 ms across the five artifacts;
  rebuilding gallery metadata about 31 ms. Neither alone explains the whole delay.
  Source processing runs synchronously inside the ASGI request coroutine and can
  delay other requests while composing the grammar.

No runtime optimization or dependency edits made. Proposed next scope: declare
only required page collections; prepare reusable verified grammar per collection
composition without sharing mutable builder/Data state; apply an explicit cache
policy to immutable build-ID asset URLs. Preserve artifact integrity checks and
class/instance override semantics. Implementation and before/after browser
verification remain pending owner confirmation. No publication or release.

## 2065 — Detachable Code panel feasibility (2026-10-25)

Owner requests verification of state-preserving detachment, starting with Code
as a third tab that can be dragged into a floating window and reattached.
This approves the feature direction; public parameter naming remains proposed.

Legacy `genro_dom.js:onDetach` keeps the original Source node, replaces its DOM
with a placeholder, moves that DOM into the floating widget, and restores it on
hide. It does not transfer the original Source subtree to a new Source parent.

Current core findings: renderer records and bindings remain owned by Source.
SelectedContainer projects stable light-DOM children through named slots, but
selection currently hides every nonselected viewport and does not know detached
panels. Window requires exactly one framePane. Ordinary DOM reparenting triggers
CodeMirror reconnect and recreates its editor instance. Source delete/insert
would also invoke cleanup and is inappropriate for retaining a live panel.

An isolated JSDOM probe against the actual core confirms three slot-projection
round trips preserve editor identity, DOM parent, selection and undo history;
Undo still writes Data and subsequent Data writes reach the editor. The same
probe confirms ordinary DOM reparenting recreates CodeMirror. Evidence in the
primary workspace: `temp/detachable-panel-review/`. This verifies the projection
primitive only, not a finished floating feature or browser focus/iframe behavior.

Proposed next contract: `detachable=True` on a tab's contentPane. Keep Source and
content DOM ownership fixed, transfer only presentation, retain a tab entry for
recall, and use the shared floating/window behavior. Drag or an explicit detach
button opens it; reattach or window close returns it. Window-frame integration,
selection while detached, focus, ancestor hide/dispose and browser qualification
still need implementation. Do not duplicate window mechanics in the gallery.
No framework feature, gallery migration or deployment performed in this review.

## 2160 — DOMPurify advisory assessment (2026-10-25)

Owner answered “ok” to “Procedo con la verifica di DOMPurify?”. This slice assesses exposure and tests the patched dependency in isolation; it does not record approval of a release or deployment. Maintained manifests remain unchanged. The minimal proposed update is dompurify 3.4.16 → 3.4.17.

All three reported advisories identify 3.4.17 as patched, matching the npm latest tag checked today:
- [GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7): SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES, DOM-returning mode, attached shadow-root input and downstream template evaluation are required. Gramlot never enables SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES and supplies strings to the sanitizer.
- [GHSA-mrv2-3pqr-j5jr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrv2-3pqr-j5jr): IN_PLACE with hooks detaching other nodes is required. Gramlot uses neither IN_PLACE nor sanitizer hooks.
- [GHSA-c6gr-qvv4-5v3f](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c6gr-qvv4-5v3f): XHTML parsing with allowed SVG animation is required. Gramlot uses HTML profiles and does not configure XHTML parsing or SVG animation allowlists.

The three core consumers are border-container drawer labels, structured tree captions and optional embedded Markdown HTML. Drawer/tree sanitization returns a fragment; Markdown returns a string. Their existing HTML formatting contract remains intact. Inspection found no current core path meeting the reported exploit conditions. This is a bounded finding for these advisories and configurations, not a blanket security guarantee for custom collections or all attacks.

Verification on consolidated c0c61b3: 69 affected-component tests passed with 3.4.16; installing 3.4.17 with --no-save/--no-package-lock changed only that installed package, leaving the manifest hash unchanged. The runtime build and complete 1,067-test JavaScript suite passed with 3.4.17, zero failures/skips. npm reported zero vulnerabilities for the installed dependency set. Existing regressions check safe formatting plus removal of scripts, event attributes, javascript URLs and disallowed controls in all three consumers, including reactive drawer updates and tree highlighting. No new browser qualification is claimed.

Recommendation: consolidate the one-line dependency update and rebuild distributable bundles before a future release/deployment. <a id="gc-070-2185"></a>
## 2185 — IndexPage ownership clarified before implementation (2026-10-25)

During the requested point-by-point explanation, the owner explicitly prohibits
storing data or instance references on Logic. The parent IndexPage owns Source
and Data; iframe pages each own separate Gramlot/Source/Data instances. Gramlot
may itself retain state for its own framework responsibilities. A parent iframe
registry is a possible example, not an instruction to introduce a new registry.
Recorded in GC-000, Logic, iframe pages and Gramlot-owned runtime state, and its
mirror. IndexLogic.this.index is therefore an ownership violation independently
of whether the current per-mount callbacks collide. No IndexPage runtime change,
new registry, test or deployment in this clarification step. Next: inspect existing
iframe/runtime ownership and propose the bounded Source/Data allocation without
reopening the prohibition on mutable Logic state.

## 2195 — Index load outcomes and gallery indicator (2026-10-25)

Owner confirmed “si” to completing `onLoad` with `cancelled` and separating load

also settles its pending run and removes its listeners after such an error.
